channel.title: Olive Oil Times - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Olive Oil Times (oliveoiltimes.com)

item.title: On Stromboli, Olive Trees Help Restore Land, Community and Tradition
item.description: A community-led olive cultivation project on Stromboli is restoring terraces, stabilizing slopes and reconnecting residents with the island’s agricultural heritage.

item.title: Study Finds Virgin Olive Oil Linked to Better Gut Health and Slower Cognitive Decline
item.description: New research suggests that virgin and extra virgin olive oil may support brain health by shaping the gut microbiota, while refined oils show weaker effects.

item.title: Jordan Expands Tunisian Olive Oil Imports as Drought Squeezes Local Supply
item.description: Jordan has approved imports of 10,000 tons of Tunisian olive oil as the country faces sharply reduced production following prolonged drought.

item.title: Extreme Weather Fuels Volatility Across the Global Olive Oil Market
item.description: Localized climate extremes are increasingly disrupting olive harvests, driving price volatility and reshaping trade flows across the global market.

item.title: European Table Olive Groups Push Back on EU-Mercosur Tariff Terms
item.description: Spanish, Italian and Greek table olive associations say EU-Mercosur terms would phase out duties on Mercosur olives entering Europe while leaving tariffs on European exports to South America in place.

item.title: Early NYIOOC Award Highlights Montenegro’s Growing Inland Olive Sector
item.description: Balša Baletić, an olive grower in Zeta near Podgorica, earned a Silver Award at the NYIOOC World Olive Oil Competition for Oro, a blend of Oblica, Istarska bjelica, Leccino and Pendolino.

item.title: Accademia Olearia Builds on Sardinia’s Heritage with Quality-Driven Growth
item.description: The Sardinian producer is increasing plantings across five municipalities and updating its milling line, while maintaining wide grove spacing and circular reuse of byproducts.

item.title: Morocco’s Olive Harvest Races Ahead as Rain, Cold and Labor Shortages Tighten the Window
item.description: Moroccan growers are accelerating the harvest after a delayed start and weeks of rain and cold. Labor shortages and higher wages are squeezing timelines even as extraction rates rise and retail olive oil prices fall.

item.title: Weeks of Rain and Flooding Slow Spain’s Olive Harvest, Threatening Output Targets
item.description: Spain’s olive harvest has been disrupted by weeks of rain and storms, prompting AEMO to trim its 2025/26 production outlook to about 1.2 million tons and warn of a lower share of extra virgin olive oil.

item.title: New Science Rewrites the Origins of Olive Cultivation in Italy
item.description: New paleogenetic and archaeobotanical techniques are challenging long-held assumptions about when olives were first cultivated in Italy, pointing to earlier and more regionalized beginnings.
